SMTO-CFG-0093 — Capability settings changed while permission was pending

GUID: 9635d88b-18c7-53a2-a224-b92043bcd1f6
Slug: capability-activation-policy-conflict
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_activation

What happened

  • While SMTO waited for your answer, this conversation's Skill settings changed, or turning the Skill on would have removed tools the task already uses. SMTO kept the newer settings and didn't turn the Skill on.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Capabilities in the message box controls, set Apply to to This conversation, and search for the Skill. Someone may have changed this conversation's or the Global Skill settings in another window while the question was open.
  2. If you still want the Skill, set it to Auto (or Always) and select Apply. Turning it on in the current settings avoids the clash between the old question and the newer settings.
  3. Send a new message asking SMTO to carry on and use that Skill. This task recorded the clash as a no, so only a new request can use the Skill.

What success looks like

  • The new request uses the Skill without this message, or shows a fresh permission question you can answer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details in this panel and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and mention whether anyone else changed Capabilities at the same time. Don't keep answering the old question; it can't be applied to the newer settings.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Committing the approved capability grant was rolled back because the conversation or global capability policy revision changed incompatibly, the prospective ceiling did not compile, or the reseeded selection would drop tools the run already accepted; the grant was recorded as conflict.

What this means

  • Prospective approved capability projection would remove already accepted tools, or revision/compile checks conflict with newer policy; the savepoint is rolled back. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • Prospective approved capability projection would remove already accepted tools, or revision/compile checks conflict with newer policy; the savepoint is rolled back.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect current policy revisions and projection differences; this shared conflict does not always prove another client edited settings.

How to fix it

  • Read the current conversation and global capability scopes (revisions, effective policy and selection) and compare them with the grant's policy_snapshot and policy_revisions. Resolve the policy change deliberately through the Capabilities editor, then start a new request so a fresh grant or accepted ceiling is created; do not replay the old grant.
  • Refresh current capability policy and the matching grant interaction before deliberately reviewing a new decision.

Retry and execution caution

  • The reported capability or interaction condition changes.

How to verify the fix

  • The grant preserves accepted tools and passes current authority checks atomically.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass frozen authority, operation permissions or credential requirements.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
